items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish.
lines: Why does everything cost nine ninety-nine? Because your brain reads it as nine dollars.
It's called the left-digit effect. You read a price left to right, and the first digit sticks.
Ten dollars feels like ten. Nine ninety-nine feels like nine-something. One cent moves a whole dollar in your head.
It even works on cars. Across twenty-two million auction sales, used cars sold for about two hundred dollars less once the odometer crossed a ten thousand mile mark.
But here's the weird part. In one experiment, a dress sold better at thirty-nine dollars than at thirty-four.
Cheaper, and fewer buyers. Why? Years of sales taught us that a nine means bargain.
That's the mirage: the nine isn't a discount. It's a signal that feels like one.
So round up. Nine ninety-nine is ten dollars.
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
